_contract: Authored by Tasklet 2026-08-16 natively to contract v3, mirroring the Dubai v3 fleet-investors gold master per the international addendum (Bahrain run — tourism-weighted utilization stack, 12-hour modeled service day). Sources: bahrain/REVENUE-INPUTS-BAHRAIN.md + FARE-BENCHMARKS-BAHRAIN.md + CREW-COST-BENCHMARKS-BAHRAIN.md + NODES-BAHRAIN.md + DEMAND-POOLS-BAHRAIN.md + AUTHORITY-MAP-BAHRAIN.md + SPEED-RULES-BAHRAIN.md. CONTRACT v3: only `title` (<=6 words), `value`/figures, `note` (<=140 chars, partner-clean plain English), `status` (enum: market_priced | modeled | upside), and `fn` (footnote key) render — plus verbatim copy fields (headline/subline/body/chips/cards/quantity/price). Underscore-prefixed fields NEVER reach the DOM. null/missing = render nothing. Footnotes render ONCE in a single 'Notes & assumptions' section above the contact form. Fleet financing only — equity/fundraise/counterparty content firewalls apply in full. Utilization-stack economics lead frame; upside rows are never summed into base totals; the tourism experience layer is the headline layer per the international addendum. No Bahrain revenue stack existed in research — this file computes the three scenarios from REVENUE-INPUTS/FARE/CREW inputs only, with every quantity an explicitly stated modeling assumption; all sums script-verified to $0 diff before writing. Service day modeled 06:00–18:00 everywhere (Coast Guard evening authorization pending — calm single-line treatment per instruction); the upside tier assumes NO evening hours. Berthing and insurance are UNSOURCED in Bahrain (no published rate cards) — excluded from totals and disclosed via fn13, per the sourced-figures-only rule. Sponsorship and cargo upside rates UNSOURCED — carried unpriced, upside-only. Demand pools are sourced visitor/resident flows, labeled indicative — no employer trackers exist on this run and no employer page exists. No phasing or vessel-count section: no sourced Bahrain plan exists, so none renders.

fn1.text: Experience, charter and hire pricing is positioned against Bahrain's operating water-leisure market: island day trips around BHD 20 per adult, group island charters at BHD 120–360 per outing, premium hourly hire reported at BHD 77 and up, and a five-star resort's published island escape at roughly $180 per hour.

fn2.text: Demand pool figures are indicative of demand potential along these corridors — sourced visitor, resident and ridership flows, not commitments or commercial relationships. Developer and master-plan figures render as published plans, not current facts.

fn3.text: Economics are indicative ranges with conservative defaults. Upside lines — sponsorship, island resupply, evening extension — are never included in base totals, and none carries a price until a local rate is sourced.

fn4.text: All trip times use conservative speed assumptions in marinas, channels and harbours, with open-water segments at the vessel's service speed. Navigation conduct in Bahrain is set through ministry licence conditions and Coast Guard notices; nothing beyond that framework is assumed.

fn5.text: Committed-seat and spot pricing are derived bands, not Bahrain quotes: anchored to the water-taxi's published BHD 0.8–1.5 fares, metered-taxi and ride-hail costs of BHD 2.5–4.4 for the same cross-island trip (BHD 110–194 a month commuting), and target-district incomes. The seat band runs $220–330 (about BHD 83–124) a seat-month. Pending confirmation.

fn6.text: Crew costs use a Bahrain-adapted method: local wage benchmarks for a licensed two-person crew (captain + deckhand), with social insurance, permits, medical cover and customary allowances stated as an explicit burden. The model runs at the mid benchmark of $16.80 per hour loaded; the low benchmark is $11.20.

fn7.text: Spot-seat lines are computed as fill rate × residual commute seat-legs × fare, with seats sold rounded down to whole seats; the stated seat count × fare is the exact revenue line.

fn8.text: The conservative case assumes deliberately thin fills at the bottom of every derived band and pays back in about 51 years — shown as the floor, not a financing case.

fn9.text: A 12-month operating year on warm, sheltered water. June–September heat shifts midday leisure toward morning and late-afternoon slots, and Ramadan softens daytime demand; commuter peaks run in a climate-controlled cabin. Scenario counts are annual monthly averages with those shapes absorbed.

fn10.text: Energy is priced at Bahrain's published commercial electricity tariff — about $0.085 per kWh at the marginal commercial slab, among the cheapest water in the program's markets. At the program's standard $0.30 per kWh planning rate the energy line rises about 3.5×, and every scenario remains cash-positive.

fn11.text: All figures are US dollars. Local benchmarks are cited in Bahraini dinars and convert at the pegged rate of 0.376 dinars per dollar (BHD 1 = $2.66).

fn12.text: Service hours are modeled 06:00–18:00; evening extension is subject to Coast Guard authorization. No base-case revenue line assumes evening hours.

fn13.text: Berthing and insurance are excluded from the operating totals: no published Bahrain rate cards exist for a commercial berth of this class or for passenger-vessel cover, and quotes are in progress. Both lines will reduce net when priced.

copy.headline: Own the vessels behind Bahrain's fast water network.
copy.subline: One vessel, four revenue layers. A tourism-weighted network across Manama, Muharraq, Amwaj and the southern islands that earns across the day — commuters, experiences, charters and spot seats — twelve months a year, on some of the cheapest crew and energy in the program.

Rendered honestly per instruction. Visitor and sea-arrival chips: data.gov.bh official open data (fn2 sources on the demand pool).

copy.headline: One asset. One day. Four demand layers.
copy.body: A commuter-only vessel earns in a fraction of its available hours — this network monetizes the whole modeled day, twelve months a year. Committed seats form the schedule spine; experiences and charters are the headline layer, priced inside a water-leisure market Bahrain already operates — and the crew and energy lines are structurally among the cheapest in the program.

_internal.sources: Prices: REVENUE-INPUTS-BAHRAIN.md §2–4 + FARE-BENCHMARKS-BAHRAIN.md §4 (all DERIVED bands, flagged for Jaideep). Crew: CREW-COST-BENCHMARKS-BAHRAIN.md (LOW $11.2 / MID $16.8 per crew pair-hour loaded; model runs MID per instruction, LOW carried in fn6/sensitivity). Energy: EWA non-domestic marginal slab 32 fils = $0.0851/kWh PRIMARY (ewa.bh) → N45 4.1 kWh/nm × $0.0851 = $0.3489/nm. Maintenance: $65K/yr program figure per REVENUE-INPUTS §1 (N30-class canon — N45 scaling pending, flagged). Peg 1 BHD = $2.6596.
_internal.capacity_basis: Commute capacity: 8 commute legs/day (4 AM + 4 PM within 06:00–18:00) × 20 seats × 22 workdays = 5280 seat-legs/mo. One committed seat = 44 legs/mo (22 days × 2). Residual seat-legs = 3,520 − committed × 44: 2,464 / 2,112 / 1,936 per scenario.

opex_basis.crew: Crew pair-hours per scenario (modeling assumption within the 12-hr day, max 360/mo): 220 / 290 / 350 hrs × $16.80 = $3,696 / $4,872 / $5,880. LOW-rate sensitivity ($11.20): crew line falls ~33%.
opex_basis.energy: Monthly nm per scenario (modeling assumption from line lengths × frequencies): 1,800 / 2,400 / 3,000 nm × 4.1 kWh/nm × $0.0851 = $628 / $837 / $1,047 (rounded). At $0.30/kWh planning rate: $2,214 / $2,952 / $3,690 — nets stay positive in all scenarios (fn10).
opex_basis.maintenance: $82,500/yr = $6,875/mo (N45-class, Dubai-parity basis; 2026-08-16 fix), flat across scenarios.
opex_basis.berthing_insurance: UNSOURCED in Bahrain (REVENUE-INPUTS §7 fail-closed items 1–2) — excluded from totals, disclosed via fn13 + opex row + sensitivity. Do NOT borrow US or Dubai figures.

_internal.opex_total_note: Opex per scenario (crew + energy + maintenance): $11,199 / $12,584 / $13,802 — rendered as the conservative-to-upside band. Scenario nets use per-scenario opex.

layer_pricing_basis.committed_bundles_L1: DERIVED $220/$275/$330 per seat-month (REVENUE-INPUTS §2 recommended band ≈ BHD 83–124/mo). Position: ~2.5–3× the public water-taxi monthly equivalent, at/below the BHD 110–194/mo ride-hail commute cost, ~4–5% of target-segment household income. Needs Jaideep confirmation before external quoting.
layer_pricing_basis.spot_seats_L2: $8/$10/$13 per leg (≈ BHD 3.0/3.8/4.9 — inside the FARE §4 derived bands: urban BHD 2–3, VIP BHD 4, through-ride BHD 3–5) × 10/20/30% fill of residual seat-legs. Seats rounded down (246/422/580); seat count × fare is the exact line (fn7). Southern-leg (BHD 6–10) and Hawar (BHD 12–18) fares are absorbed in the experience layer, not double-counted in L2.
layer_pricing_basis.experiences_charters_L3: Experiences $32/$40/$48 pp (= BHD 12/15/18, the FARE §4 derived Hawar-express/premium-experience band) × 20/40/60 sailings/mo × 10/12/14 seats. Charters $213/$266/$346 per hr (= BHD 80/100/130, FARE §2 derived N45 band) × 8/16/24 hrs/mo. Anchors: BHD 20 day-trip bundle, BHD 120–360 group charters, BHD 77/hr yacht-hour, $180/hr resort product — positioning anchors only, never rendered as facts.
layer_pricing_basis.sponsorship_U1: UNSOURCED rate (REVENUE-INPUTS §5) — rendered unpriced, upside-only. The Dubai $150K/yr placeholder is NOT borrowed.
layer_pricing_basis.resupply_U2: Hawar clean resupply is the city-appropriate cargo class (boat-only island, resort open — PRIMARY); rate UNSOURCED — rendered unpriced, upside-only. Daytime framing (no night ops assumed).
layer_pricing_basis.evening_extension_U3: Bahrain-specific upside line replacing Dubai's speed-relief row: evening hours pending Coast Guard authorization (fn12). Unpriced; upside tier does NOT assume it.

_internal.scenario_qa: Mid ~10.3 yr is the honest headline — Bahrain fares are ~⅓ of US/Dubai levels and cheap opex does not fully offset. Conservative is cash-positive but very slow (~80 yr) — rendered with fn8 floor language, honestly, per instruction. Upside ~4.4 yr stays inside the 12-hr day and includes NO unpriced upside lines. Cross-city comparisons never render.
_internal.maintenance_basis: 2026-08-16 parity fix: maintenance uplifted from $65K/yr (N30-class canon) to $82.5K/yr N45-class to match Dubai basis; opex/net/payback recomputed. Old figures superseded.

navier_intro.title: Meet the vessel

copy.headline: A U.S.-built electric hydrofoil.
copy.body: Navier is a U.S. builder of electric hydrofoil vessels. Its N45 Explorer carries 30 passengers at a foilborne cruise speed of about 30 knots — lifted clear of the water for a smooth ride above the wake and wash of conventional hulls. The smaller N30 Quanta carries 8. Foiling cuts energy use by up to ~90% versus a conventional planing hull, and both vessels run near-silent on electric power.

tech_chips.value: up to ~90% less than a planing hull

copy.note: A vessel is a network asset, not stranded in one market — the multi-city network is the residual-value story.
